searchText: To rephrase the ask a bit: can EIP-8141 make it clear whether and how tx type introspection should be done? Right now, it can be done either via `ORIGIN (or CALLER) == ENTRY_POINT` (as noted in the thread, not robust in all cases) or via a `STATICCALL` to a helper. Both currently seem like hacks. I see a few ways to satisfy this: 1. say it is not recommended at all and explain why in the EIP's Rationale. All contracts should dispatch between frame and non-frame paths using calldata (like many seem to do, now) 2. define `ORIGIN (or CALLER) == ENTRY_POINT` as the recommended way, declare that `ENTRY_POINT` will not be used in other contexts, and note that it can still diverge in an `eth_call` and `SENDER` frame (issue raised on the forum) 3. relax `TXPARAM(0x00)` to work in other tx types (this seems like the cheapest and most natural way out) 4. relax `TXPARAM` more broadly and let it degrade gracefully in non-frame transactions, returning some appropriate data or zeros. This is similar to how `BLOBHASH` works outside of a blob transaction. The motivation is to avoid creating a precedent where a read-only opcode halts based on tx type. In any case, an addition to the Rationale section would be welcome.

excerpts.content:
To rephrase the ask a bit: can EIP-8141 make it clear whether and how tx type introspection should be done? Right now, it can be done either via `ORIGIN (or CALLER) == ENTRY_POINT` (as noted in the thread, not robust in all cases) or via a `STATICCALL` to a helper. Both currently seem like hacks.

I see a few ways to satisfy this:
1. say it is not recommended at all and explain why in the EIP's Rationale. All contracts should dispatch between frame and non-frame paths using calldata (like many seem to do, now)
2. define `ORIGIN (or CALLER) == ENTRY_POINT` as the recommended way, declare that `ENTRY_POINT` will not be used in other contexts, and note that it can still diverge in an `eth_call` and `SENDER` frame (issue raised on the forum)
3. relax `TXPARAM(0x00)` to work in other tx types (this seems like the cheapest and most natural way out)
4. relax `TXPARAM` more broadly and let it degrade gracefully in non-frame transactions, returning some appropriate data or zeros. This is similar to how `BLOBHASH` works outside of a blob transaction. The motivation is to avoid creating a precedent where a read-only opcode halts based on tx type.

In any case, an addition to the Rationale section would be welcome.
